'''Anantanarayanan Raman''' is a Professor of Ecology with [[Charles Sturt University]], NSW<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anantanarayanan Raman|url=https://researchoutput.csu.edu.au/en/persons/aramancsueduau|access-date=2021-06-14|website=Charles Sturt University Research Output|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614160251/https://researchoutput.csu.edu.au/en/persons/aramancsueduau|archive-date=2021-06-14}}</ref> and a scientist with [[CSIRO]], Australia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=People – Ecosystem Change Ecology|url=https://ecosystemchangeecology.org/people/|access-date=2021-06-14|website=ecosystemchangeecology.org}}</ref>

== Education ==
Raman received his bachelor's degree in biology from [[Loyola College, Chennai|Loyola College]], Madras followed by a master's degree in biology from [[Presidency College, Chennai|Presidency College]], Madras, and PhD & DSc degrees in ecology from [[Madras University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Seckbach|first1=Joseph|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Rl0ER01ZI8cC&q=anantanarayanan+raman+fulbrightraman&pg=PA120|title=All Flesh Is Grass: Plant-Animal Interrelationships|last2=Dubinsky|first2=Zvy|date=11 October 2010|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-90-481-9316-5|language=en}}</ref> As a graduate student, he researched at the [[Louis Pasteur University|Université Louis Pasteur, France]], on the nutritional physiology of gall-inducing [[Tubulifera]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Taptamani|first1=Heishnam|last2=Varatharajan|first2=Rameiyer|last3=Raman|first3=Anantanarayanan|date=15 May 2012|title=Biology of leaf gall-inducing Thlibothrips manipurenis Muraleedharan, 1982 on Ardisia sp. (Myrsinaceae) in north-eastern India (Thysanoptera: Tubulifera: Phlaeothripidae).|url=https://www.contributions-to-entomology.org/article/view/1806|journal=Beiträge zur Entomologie = Contributions to Entomology|volume=62|issue=1|pages=69–76|doi=10.21248/contrib.entomol.62.1.69-76|issn=2511-6428|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Research ==
Raman received a [[Fulbright Award]]<ref name=":0" /> in 1990 to work with [[Warren Abrahamson|Warren G. Abrahamson]], of [[Bucknell University]] on population ecology and evaluated energetics using the ''Solidago–Rhopalomyia'' system.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Raman|first=Anantanarayanan|date=May 2003|title=Cecidogenetic Behavior of some gall-inducing thrips, psyllids, coccids, and gall midges, and morphogenesis of their galls|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00305316.2003.10417356|journal=Oriental Insects|language=en|volume=37|issue=1|pages=359–413|doi=10.1080/00305316.2003.10417356|s2cid=84634798|issn=0030-5316|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Raman received a [[German Academic Exchange Service|German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)]] grant<ref>{{Cite web|title=Heidelberg Alumni International - Service: Alumni Revue - September 2000: Alumni persönlich|url=https://www.alumni.uni-heidelberg.de/revue/revue_pers_1_2000.html|access-date=2021-06-15|website=alumni.uni-heidelberg.de}}</ref> to study the aseptic dual culture technique using ''Pemphigus'' and its primary host ''Populus'' and secondary host ''Taraxacum,'' and hypersensitive responses among species of ''Vitis'' to infestations of ''Daktulusphairia vitifoliae''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Raman|first1=Anantanarayanan|last2=Beiderbeck|first2=Rolf|last3=Herth|first3=Werner|date=August 2009|title=Early subcellular responses of susceptible and resistant Vitis taxa to feeding by grape phylloxera Daktulosphaira vitifoliae|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00035-009-0054-4|journal=Botanica Helvetica|language=en|volume=119|issue=1|pages=31–39|doi=10.1007/s00035-009-0054-4|s2cid=34820953|issn=0253-1453|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Raman collaborated with Rolf Beiderbeck of [[Ruprecht-Karls-Universitat Heidelberg|Rurpecht–Karls Universität]], to work on a protocol for raising plant‑feeding insects on aseptically‑grown tissue callus of its host plant, using the ''Trialeyrodes–Stellaria'' system.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Raman|first1=A.|last2=Beiderbeck|first2=R.|date=12 January 1992|title=Aseptic dual culture of the greenhouse whitefly, Trialeurodes vaporariorum Westwood (Hom., Aleyrodidae) and its host, Stellaria media (L.) Vill. (Caryophyllaceae)|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1111/j.1439-0418.1992.tb00662.x|journal=Journal of Applied Entomology|language=en|volume=113|issue=1–5|pages=252–257|doi=10.1111/j.1439-0418.1992.tb00662.x|s2cid=84919508|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2000, he received the [[Ian Potter Foundation]]’s award<ref name=":1" /> and visited the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]], to evaluate the nutrient mobilisation in the moth-induced galls of the [[parthenium]] weed using stable [[isotope mass spectrometry]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Raman|first1=A.|last2=Madhavan|first2=S.|last3=Florentine|first3=S.K.|last4=Dhileepan|first4=K.|date=May 2006|title=Metabolite mobilization in the stem galls of Parthenium hysterophorus induced by Epiblema strenuana inferred from the signatures of isotopic carbon and nitrogen and concentrations of total non-structural carbohydrates|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1111/j.1570-7458.2006.00403.x|journal=Entomologia Experimentalis et Applicata|language=en|volume=119|issue=2|pages=101–107|doi=10.1111/j.1570-7458.2006.00403.x|bibcode=2006EEApp.119..101R |hdl=1959.17/56858|s2cid=84501345|issn=0013-8703}}</ref> Raman received an [[Australian Academy of Science]] fellowship<ref>{{Cite web|last=Raman|first=Anantanarayanan|date=25 January 2008|title=Workshop on Scientific writing for professional journals and theses|url=http://www.entomol.nchu.edu.tw/dept/teachers/mmyang/download/%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%B8%E5%AF%AB%E4%BD%9C%E7%A0%94%E7%BF%92%E6%9C%83%E5%85%AC%E5%91%8A.pdf|access-date=15 June 2021|website=|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616043037/http://www.entomol.nchu.edu.tw/dept/teachers/mmyang/download/%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%B8%E5%AF%AB%E4%BD%9C%E7%A0%94%E7%BF%92%E6%9C%83%E5%85%AC%E5%91%8A.pdf|archive-date=2021-06-16}}</ref> to visit the [[National Chung Hsing University]], Taiwan to study the nutritional ecology of insects invading ''[[Machilus Thunbergii]].''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pan|first1=Liang-Yu|last2=Chen|first2=Wen-Neng|last3=Chiu|first3=Shau-Ting|last4=Raman|first4=Anantanarayanan|last5=Chiang|first5=Tung-Chuang|last6=Yang|first6=Man-Miao|date=June 2015|title=Is a Gall an Extended Phenotype of the Inducing Insect? A Comparative Study of Selected Morphological and Physiological Traits of Leaf and Stem Galls on Machilus thunbergii (Lauraceae) Induced by Five Species of Daphnephila (Diptera: Cecidomyiidae) in Northeastern Taiwan|url=http://www.bioone.org/doi/10.2108/zs140244|journal=Zoological Science|language=en|volume=32|issue=3|pages=314–321|doi=10.2108/zs140244|pmid=26003988|s2cid=207285754|issn=0289-0003|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Muthiah|first=S.|date=16 April 2018|title=The Serbian connection|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/society/history-and-culture/tafes-connection-with-industrija-masina-i-traktora/article23555831.ece|access-date=2021-06-14|issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Raman was invited by the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA), on a [[Vulimiri Ramalingaswami]] Fellowship,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy News|url=https://1library.net/document/zkw6kxpz-academy-news.html|access-date=2021-06-14|website=1library.net|language=en}}</ref> through which he conducted workshops and training programs at Indian universities.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Calicut varsity to host GIAN programme|url=https://researchoutput.csu.edu.au/en/clippings/calicut-varsity-to-host-gian-programme|access-date=2021-06-14|website=Charles Sturt University Research Output|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=25 February 2019|title=Calicut varsity to host GIAN programme|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/calicut-varsity-to-host-gian-programme/article26368290.ece|access-date=2021-06-14|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

== Science history of Madras (Chennai) city and India ==
Raman became interested in chronicling the growth of science in India, particularly that of Madras city, especially that occurred between 1650 and 1947 AD. Raman continues to publish articles related to science history, in professional journals, such as ''[[Current Science]]'' (Bangalore)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Raman |first=Anantanarayanan |date=7 May 2020 |title=Marble-like chûnnam in the 18th- and 19th-century Madras Presidency |journal=Indian Journal of History of Science |volume=55 |issue=1 |doi=10.16943/ijhs/2020/v55i1/152340 |s2cid=219409432 |issn=0019-5235|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Raman |first1=Ramya |last2=Raman |first2=Anantanarayanan |date=25 March 2018 |title=Medical Stores in 1865, Pharmacist Training and Pharmacopoeias in India Until the Launch of the Indian Pharmacopoeia in 1955 |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.18520/cs/v114/i06/1358-1366 |journal=Current Science |volume=114 |issue=6 |pages=1358 |doi=10.18520/cs/v114/i06/1358-1366 |issn=0011-3891|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Raman |first=Anantanarayanan |date=2 September 2020 |title=G.M.M.C. Diploma of the Madras Medical College, 1847–1863 |journal=Indian Journal of History of Science |volume=55 |issue=2 |doi=10.16943/ijhs/2020/v55i2/154673 |s2cid=225312246 |issn=0019-5235|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Raman |first=Anantanarayanan |date=1 September 2018 |title=Internationalization of Indian Higher-Education |journal=Current Science |volume=115 |issue=5 |pages=809 |doi=10.18520/cs/v115/i5/809-809 |s2cid=108835049 |issn=0011-3891|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Raman |first=Anantanarayanan |date=25 May 2018 |title=Wool-Pile Carpets in Colonial Madras and the Lost Saidapet Woolly-Sheep Breed in Madras of the 1870s |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.18520/cs/v114/i10/2201-2204 |journal=Current Science |volume=114 |issue=10 |pages=2201 |doi=10.18520/cs/v114/i10/2201-2204 |issn=0011-3891|url-access=subscription }}</ref>., ''Indian Journal of the History of Science'' ([[Indian National Science Academy]]), New Delhi),<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Raman |first1=Ramya |last2=Raman |first2=Anantanarayanan |date=1 January 2017 |title=Amoebic Dysentery and Introduction of Emetine Source Carapichea ipecacacuanha into Indian Subcontinent |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.16943/ijhs/2017/v52i1/41300 |journal=Indian Journal of History of Science |volume=52 |issue=1 |doi=10.16943/ijhs/2017/v52i1/41300
